newsitem.title: UK: Clyde rejects Gulf Canada bid as too low.
newsitem.headline: Clyde rejects Gulf Canada bid as too low.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc advised its shareholders Sunday to reject a hostile 432 million sterling ($732 million) bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd., saying the offer drastically undervalued the company.
"Gulf Canada's offer dramatically undervalues Clyde on a cash flow multiple basis," Clyde Chairman Malcolm Gourlay said in an interview.
"An independent Clyde will deliver a far better return for our shareholders than this low offer. It's fairly much of a no-brainer to reject this offer."

Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence ($1.78) a share was considered too low by many analysts when it was launched Dec. 18. Shares in Clyde closed at 118 pence ($2.00) in London Friday, indicating the market's belief that Gulf Canada would have to increase its offer to clinch a deal.
Gourlay declined to specify what he would consider a fairer valuation for his company.

Roy Franklin, Clyde's managing director, said his company had been transformed in the past three years, and its strategy would create far greater value for shareholders than Gulf Canada's attempted takeover.
"Production, reserves, reported cash flow and reported profit have all consistently risen to record levels, and we've now got a business that is really performing," he said in an interview.

Before its bid in December, Gulf had made no secret of the fact that it was seeking an international acquisition that would bring with it a new core area to complement its extensive operations in Canada and Indonesia.
Clyde's activities in the North Sea and Australia made a good fit, analysts said.
